articles.title: Drake Maye injury mystery: Bill Simmons blasts Patriots as silence over QB's condition fuels season-ending fears
articles.summary: The New England Patriots are facing growing uncertainty over Drake Maye's health after the quarterback suffered a right ankle injury against the Detroit
articles.body: The New England Patriots are facing growing uncertainty over Drake Maye's health after the quarterback suffered a right ankle injury against the Detroit Lions. More than just another setback in a difficult season, the injury has raised fears that New England could lose its most important player for an extended period. The lack of a clear medical update has also frustrated Bill Simmons, who questioned why the Patriots had not confirmed whether Maye suffered a fracture. With the playoffs still within reach, the uncertainty is becoming a problem of its own.Bill Simmons takes aim at Patriots over Drake Maye injury updateMaye's injury came at a particularly bad time for New England. The quarterback went down during the opening drive of the Patriots' November 15 game against Detroit in Munich. Lions defensive end Aidan Hutchinson brought him down, leaving Maye in visible discomfort. He did not return, and the Patriots went on to lose 35-10.The defeat was damaging enough, but the uncertainty surrounding Maye quickly became the bigger talking point. Reports indicated that the Patriots feared a possible fracture, which could keep the young quarterback out for the remainder of the season.That possibility did not sit well with Simmons. The longtime Patriots supporter took to social media and questioned why the organization had not provided a straightforward answer.“Getting close to noon ET on Tuesday – how do we not know if Drake Maye has a fractured ankle yet? The injury happened over 48 hours ago. This one seems like a pretty simple yes or no,” Simmons tweeted.His frustration reflects what many New England fans are likely feeling. They are not simply waiting for a return date. They want to know whether their franchise quarterback has suffered an injury that could change the direction of the entire campaign.Mike Vrabel explains delay as Patriots prepare for life without Drake MayeHead coach Mike Vrabel addressed the situation on November 16 but stopped short of confirming the diagnosis. Maye had remained in Germany for further medical checks before travelling back to the United States with members of the Patriots' medical staff.Vrabel explained why the team was holding back information.“I'm not going to make any comments about his status until he gets back here. He's en route back here. He stayed with a few of our people, and they're en route back here. So, once he gets back here, and our people are able to visit with him again and talk with him again, I think we'll have more to offer. But I wouldn't imagine him being available when we come out of the bye.”That last sentence offered little comfort. Vrabel effectively ruled out Maye for the November 29 meeting with the Los Angeles Chargers, even without confirming how serious the ankle damage was.New England now has to consider its options. Tommy DeVito could take over, while Behren Morton is another possibility. The Patriots may also explore outside help during their bye week.There is no reason to rush Maye back before he is ready. But the longer the diagnosis remains unclear, the harder it becomes for New England to plan its next move. At 5-5, the Patriots need answers quickly, and the most important one concerns the health of their quarterback.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Travis Kelce Reacts to 'Dirty Tackle' Question After Injury on Hit from Falcons Player in New Video
articles.summary: Kansas City Chiefs tight end Travis Kelce is in good spirits after taking a hit to his already-injured ankle in Sunday's win over the Atlanta Falcons.
articles.body:
Kansas City Chiefs tight end Travis Kelce is in good spirits after taking a hit to his already-injured ankle in Sunday's win over the Atlanta Falcons.

During this week's episode of the New Heights podcast (52:00 mark), Kelce's brother, Jason, read a fan question that argued that Falcons safety DeMarcco Hellams made an "intentionally dirty tackle" by targeting the 37-year-old's ankle. However, the three-time Super Bowl champion didn't see it that way.

"I don't know if that was the case; the way he tackled me… I just got caught in a bad position," Kelce said. "You know, that's football. And on the flip side, you know, if it was a quote-unquote intentional, you know, extra grab and turn of the ankle, you know, it's just part of it. I don't think it was, you know, crazy enough for it to get a flag or it to be a fine or anything like that. Obviously, in the moment, I thought it was, because it hurt like hell."

Kelce originally injured his ankle in Kansas City's Week 6 win over the Los Angeles Chargers. He was hurt again in the first quarter against Atlanta, finishing with just two catches for 30 yards in the 35-13 win.

Despite the injury, Kelce said he plans to be on the field when the Chiefs (7-2) return to action against the Arizona Cardinals (3-7) on Sunday.

"I'm ready to rock and roll this week," he said. "It's one of those things where once you turn it in at the beginning of the year, you've just got to deal with the high-ankle sprain and the process it takes to heal. When you're battling through week to week trying to get it to 100%, it's going to be a lot slower than just taking time off. But I love playing this game, and if I'm out there on a good ankle or a bad ankle, it doesn't f--king matter to me. I'm out there because I love this game. I signed up for this thing to be out there putting my heart on the line and my body on the line for my teammates."

articles.title: NFL Draft 2027 Scouting Report for Texas S Jelani McDonald
articles.summary: Jelani McDonald is the best tackling safety in this class and plays the run like he's a real linebacker in the secondary. He's an experienced member of the Longhorns' defense, and his pre- and post-snap communication puts players in the right spot and helps align coverage during the play. With his exceptional size and length, McDonald can play several roles in the defense at a high level.
articles.body:
Jelani McDonald is the best tackling safety in this class and plays the run like he's a real linebacker in the secondary. He's an experienced member of the Longhorns' defense, and his pre- and post-snap communication puts players in the right spot and helps align coverage during the play. With his exceptional size and length, McDonald can play several roles in the defense at a high level.

The 4- star recruit could have declared for the 2026 NFL Draft after his breakout junior season, which included three picks and three passes defended, but he chose to return to help Texas win a National Championship. His leadership shows up every snap and has been essential to the Longhorns' defense.

Dan has covered the Kansas City Chiefs and the NFL Draft since 2019 while contributing for RGR Football. Most recently, he spent the 2025 draft cycle at The Draft Network and is entering his first season in our scouting department.

Jelani McDonald's eye discipline is an elite trait and takes him to the football regularly. He rarely falls for misdirection, especially in the run game.

He's as sure a tackler as they come and is a huge plus against the run and as an escape valve.

Can wear a lot of different hats for a defense, and his trigger downhill keeps him involved at every level.

His instincts and route recognition take away routes, forcing the quarterback into checkdowns.

A high-level communicator, he displays his knowledge, helping his teammates execute their assignments as well as his own.

He plays with excellent intermediate depth in zone and constricts the middle of the field with his football IQ and length.

McDonald is not a natural post safety, and his recovery speed/range can be attacked down the field.

There are transitional hitch concerns when he has to turn and run due to hip tightness.

He'll take a few aggressive angles in man coverage per game where receivers can take advantage and get open.

PLAYSTYLE FAMILY : In the Jevon Holland mold, McDonald is an elite run defender with strong instincts and movement skills for his size. He does his best work closer to the line of scrimmage and in coverage in the middle of the field.

articles.title: “Every chapter has taught me something”: Tyreek Hill’s words after Dolphins exit resurface as his  comeback remains uncertain
articles.summary: Tyreek Hill, the 32 year old wide receiver, is facing an uncertain future in the league while he is being linked to several teams in the league.
articles.body: Tyreek Hill, the 32 year old wide receiver, is facing an uncertain future in the league while he is being linked to several teams in the league. Though the star wide receiver has not signed a deal yet, his words on when he left the Miami Dolphins have resurfaced.Tyreek Hill’s words on leaving the Miami Dolphins resurface amid the uncertainty in his careerEarlier this year, in February, Tyreek Hill had taken to his social media to make a post about bidding goodbye to his former team, the Miami Dolphins, after they ended up releasing him.The popular wide receiver made a post that read as, “The Journey Don’t Stop✌🏿 From the bottom of my heart, Thank You To the entire @miamidolphins organization, my teammates, the staff, and most importantly Fins Nation, for an unforgettable 4 years. From the moment I landed in Miami, I felt the Love. You believed in me. You pushed me. You celebrated with me. These past few years have been some of the most meaningful of my life and career. To my brothers in the locker room who have come and gone — Thank You for the wins, the Ls, the memories, the sacrifices. We built something special, together, for the city of Miami.”The post added, “Every chapter in life has taught me something. This one taught me leadership, resilience, and mostly gratitude. The love I have for this game is unexplainable. And right now, this off season, for the first time ever, The Cheetah is all the way turned up and locked in. Focused. The Cheetah don’t slow down. Ever. So to everyone wondering what’s next… just wait on it. The Cheetah will be back…Born Again. Major Love 305. 🐆✌🏿”Tyreek Hill’s words on leaving the Miami Dolphins resurfaces at a time when there are serious concerns about his health.For the unversed, the Miami Dolphins released wide receiver Tyreek Hill on February 16, 2026, primarily to clear $22.8 million in salary cap space as part of a broader roster rebuild.Along with Tyreek Hill, several other veterans including Bradley Chubb, James Daniels, and Nick Westbrook-Ikhine were also released to free up cap room.Shortly after Tyreek Hill sustained brutal injuries last year, he had reflected on how retirement could be an option for him.However, a year later, it seems the 32 year old free agent has dismissed those claims and is fully focused on getting back to the field.When can Tyreek Hill return to the field?While his agent, Drew Rosenhaus, has assured that he has been having conversations with several teams about his potential return to the field, nothing has been confirmed yet.Though there were strong rumors about a potential reunion with the Kansas City Chiefs, the Pittsburgh Steelers have also emerged as another option for him.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: NFL Draft 2027 Scouting Report for LSU S Ty Benefield
articles.summary: Ty Benefield carries a hit stick in his pocket and always looks to activate it downhill against the offense. After transferring from Boise State over the summer, he's taken on a leadership role for the Tigers' defense and sets the tone with the effort and impact he brings against the run. He's an excellent athlete for his size, with the tools to handle multiple roles across the defense.
articles.body:
Ty Benefield carries a hit stick in his pocket and always looks to activate it downhill against the offense. After transferring from Boise State over the summer, he's taken on a leadership role for the Tigers' defense and sets the tone with the effort and impact he brings against the run. He's an excellent athlete for his size, with the tools to handle multiple roles across the defense.

The former 3- star recruit to Boise State took on a brand new challenge entering the SEC this season and has answered the bell with his physicality and ownership of his play. The counting stats won't be as impressive as his junior season, but the experience he's getting against this level of competition will help him as he looks to make it to the NFL.

Dan has covered the Kansas City Chiefs and the NFL Draft since 2019 while contributing for RGR Football. Most recently, he spent the 2025 draft cycle at The Draft Network and is entering his first season in our scouting department.

Benefield reads and reacts downhill against screens and runs with authority. Quick trigger turns into big hits while filling lanes regularly.

His aggression allows him to play more box snaps and even in the big nickel with the attitude to contribute in the run game.

Reads the seams and middle of the field well with singular routes and takes away in breakers routinely.

Will man up against tight ends and has the physicality with great length to impact the catch point.

Benefield's overaggressive playstyle leads to poor angles in pursuit of the football in every aspect.

A big hitter, but doesn't tackle with proper technique often and will miss too many tackles.

The 6'3", 216-pound safety struggles with eye discipline and matching quarterback eyes to routes in space.

Processing speed in the box can be slow, giving the ball carrier easier access to space and creating arm tackles.

PLAYSTYLE FAMILY : Benefield is a tall and long safety who has built a reputation as a hard hitter with unique athletic gifts for his size. He plays like Bernard Pollard, without the sure tackling.

articles.title: Brandon Aiyuk's Potential 49ers Return, Injury Status Discussed by Agent in Video Amid NFL Rumors
articles.summary: Brandon Aiyuk is healthy but not currently anticipating another chance to play for the San Francisco 49ers, his agent Drew Rosenhaus told Dianna Russini on Wednesday's episode of The Russini Report.
articles.body:
Brandon Aiyuk is healthy but not currently anticipating another chance to play for the San Francisco 49ers, his agent Drew Rosenhaus told Dianna Russini on Wednesday's episode of The Russini Report.

"He is 100 percent healthy right now, and in shape, and working out full-force, and he is absolutely ready to go back to play football," Rosenhaus said around the 8:00 mark of the podcast.

Rosenhaus added, however, that "Brandon and I have not seriously discussed him returning to the Niners just because we are not sure that that is an option."

The NFL granted Aiyuk reinstatement Nov. 9 while giving the 49ers until Nov. 24 to reinstate him to the 53-man roster.

The 49ers could look to cut or trade Aiyuk ahead of that deadline after indicating they don't expect the wide receiver to take another snap for San Francisco.

Niners coach Kyle Shanahan said after the NFL's decision Aiyuk's reinstatement was "administrative stuff" that meant "absolutely nothing to our team."

"The Niners have not been bashful in saying publicly that they're not planning on him coming back... Our gut feeling is that he'll become a free agent, and we'll have options," Rosenhaus told Russini.

Rosenhaus said he isn't allowed to speak with under teams while Aiyuk remains under contract with the Niners, but feels Aiyuk might work out for multiple teams after hitting free agency.

"He did pass all of the physicals that the 49ers gave him. He had MRIs, and X-rays, and a physical exam, and he did really well. There were no issues... He would like to get out there and start playing as soon as possible," Rosenhaus said.

The Niners started stripping guarantees from Aiyuk's contract amid a dispute over how the wide receiver was conducting rehab from the knee injury that ended his 2024 season.

After sitting out the entirety of the 2025 campaign, Aiyuk frequently publicly criticized the 49ers and the NFLPA while expressing his desire to play for the Washington Commanders on social media.

ESPN's Adam Schefter and Ian Rapoport reported ahead of the trade deadline earlier this month the Commanders "haven't completed abandoned the idea" of acquiring Aiyuk, but that any deal would have to be preceded by "discussions with multiple people."

Other teams in need of wide receiving help, such as the Los Angeles Rams or Kansas City Chiefs, could also consider bringing in Aiyuk for a workout. When that could take place will depend on how long the Niners delay their decision regarding how to handle Aiyuk's remaining contract.

articles.title: Robert Pattinson’s James Bond casting sparks fake announcements linking Twilight star to New England Patriots and Houston Texans
articles.summary: The New England Patriots lost Drake Maye to a suspected season-ending injury - after a Week 10 loss to the Detroit Lions.
articles.body: The New England Patriots lost Drake Maye to a suspected season-ending injury - after a Week 10 loss to the Detroit Lions. On the other hand, the Houston Texans, though placed second in the AFC South division, are still struggling with a 3-6 record.The other two teams that rank behind them - Indianapolis Colts and Tennessee Titans are not great ones either: Colts [3-7] and Titans [1-8]. So, to help these midseason-suffering NFL teams, a new candidate was reportedly linked to them. Enter - Robert Pattinson. Who would have thought?Robert Pattinson and New England Patriots connectionThe Twilight star was brought into the NFL discussion because he’s reportedly taking everybody else’s job after being named the next James Bond, according to AS USA’s Jennifer Bubel.The New England Patriots connection reportedly came from a post by Onyx Odds. They wrote, “REPORT: The Patriots are naming Robert Pattinson their starting QB for the rest of the season.”They attached an image of the 40-year-old British actor in a Patriots jersey with the caption: “ALERT: Patriots signing Robert Pattinson.” The post was made to look as real as possible.A user quickly commented, “AI won’t take your job, Robert Pattinson will.” Another said, “Not gonna lie, I feel like he could actually play quarterback.” A post read, “Now football has just gotten interesting.”Another chimed in, “Robert Pattinson is in line to play Tom Brady for a biopic at this rate. Legendary run we’re witnessing.” A user wrote, “I hear he’s playing QB and WR1.”Another commented, “Finally a QB with range.” A post read, “Better than [San Francisco 49ers QB] Mac Jones.” Another said, “He looks like a nice quarterback. Good luck, Robert.”Robert Pattinson and Houston Texans connectionBack in 2011, Houston was Robert Pattinson’s favorite city in America. “I love Houston. It’s just, I don’t know, I had a really good time there,” he said via Houston Press in 2011. He came to town in 2010 and spent most of his night in Notsuoh, playing music and hanging out. So that’s the Pattinson-Houston connection.As for the real situation with the Texans? Their quarterback, CJ Stroud, has great individual stats, but his stats aren’t helping the team grab visible wins. However, their latest Week 10 loss to the Cleveland Browns 24-27 will not be holding CJ Stroud or his team down.“What else are we going to do? Cry about it and hold our heads down? Woe is us, woe is the team? I don’t believe in that,” Stroud told reporters Tuesday [Nov. 17].“It sucks, yeah. I’m not the happiest camper, but I think the motivated me is one of the best me’s that I’ve seen. I think even as a team the motivated Texans is a scary team.”Stroud continued, “It’s up to us. We don’t need anybody else. That’s my message to the guys. We don’t need anybody else to have faith in us or to think that we can do this or can’t do this. It doesn’t really matter. We’re the ones on the field making plays, and we have the opportunity.Everybody can have an opinion, but when you have the opportunity, you’ve got to go and do it, and I think it just starts one thing at a time.”So, clearly Houston doesn’t need Robert Pattinson as their offensive coordinator to save them. CJ Stroud and company will do that for themselves. The fake announcements and connections can now finally rest.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.body:
The Minnesota Vikings are trying to bring Mexico City to suburban Saint Paul in order to prepare their players for the trip to Estadio Azteca in Week 11.

The team set up a temporary training facility that simulates competing at altitude:

Mexico City is more than 7,000 feet above sea level, and the thin air will present a challenge to members of the Vikings and San Francisco 49ers.

Fans will see Sunday which of the two strategies was more effective.

articles.title: As Cowboys strip DC Christian Parker of play-calling, Brian Schottenheimer asserts stakes: 'If we don't make the playoffs, it's a failure'
articles.summary: The remainder of the Cowboys' season will influence not only Parker's coaching future but also Schottenheimer's.
articles.body:
In Houston and Denver, the decisions took just four games this season.

Head coaches DeMeco Ryans and Sean Payton stripped their defensive and offensive coordinator of play-calling responsibilities in early October. An 0-4 start for Houston and a 2-2 start in Denver convinced each man at the helm to send his unit in a different direction.

Against that backdrop, the Dallas Cowboys stripping defensive coordinator Christian Parker of play-calling this week seems less rash. But Parker was still just 10 games into his play-calling career when Dallas transferred that responsibility to senior defensive assistant Mike Pettine, whose experience includes eight seasons as a defensive coordinator and two as head coach.

Pettine will call defensive plays beginning this week against the Tennessee Titans, Cowboys head coach Brian Schottenheimer confirmed Wednesday.

"I plan on him being the play-caller for the year," Schottenheimer added.

It's a drastic shift from the confidence and excitement that surrounded the 34-year-old Parker coming out of training camp, when a highly vocal and schematically multiple group of defenders had Dallas brass wondering whether they could solve multi-year defensive woes.

Parker has not fixed the Cowboys' defense as the unit ranks third-worst in points allowed per game (28.2) and worst in yards (393.8). But consider that last season's Cowboys ranked worst in points allowed and third-worst in yards a year after the Cowboys ranked second worst in points allowed and bottom-five in yards.

The issues predate Parker. The fix remains elusive.

Still, after ceding 46 points and a Cowboys home record-worst 584 yards to the San Francisco 49ers, Parker's role has been reduced. He will continue to run meetings and lead walkthroughs during the week even as his play-calling input will shrink to secondary.

Schottenheimer acknowledged that the urgency is high for the 4-6 group that holds just a 29% chance of making the playoffs, per Next Gen Stats projections .

"If we don't make the playoffs, it's a failure," Schottenheimer said. "The season's a failure. That's what we play for. We play to win and we play to make the playoffs, and we've got seven games left. "We need to put together a run of success."

Schottenheimer: Parker has 'very bright future here as our defense coordinator'

In aggregate, the Cowboys have produced on offense. Their 28.6 points per game rank fifth-best in the league and their 368.3 yards rank eighth.

But Dallas has not beaten a team on track to make the playoffs.

The Cowboys' run game has jelled inconsistently, and their ability to finish games deserves questions on both sides of the ball.

Even as Dallas shifts from Parker to Pettine this week, early competition will only test improvement to a degree. The 1-8 Tennessee Titans visit AT&T Stadium this week, followed by the 2-7 Philadelphia Eagles on Thanksgiving.

Then Dallas' tougher stretch will come: the Seattle Seahawks before the Cowboys' bye, followed by the Los Angeles Rams, Jacksonville Jaguars and New York Giants.

How intentional was shifting defensive play-callers before a lighter schedule stretch?

"Not at all," Schottenheimer said. "Because again, we live in the moment. This decision was based off of the last few weeks and just looking at what was best for the team and not about who you're playing."

The last few weeks, for Dallas, have featured an overtime loss against the Arizona Cardinals despite a 14-point lead early in the fourth quarter followed by a game against the trade deadline-selling Indianapolis Colts that required a fourth-quarter comeback to eke out a win.

Technically, the Cowboys lost by only 6 points on Sunday to the 49ers. But San Francisco led 38-19 early in the fourth quarter and never trailed in the second half.

At least as damaging: The 49ers scored touchdowns on plays of 74, 70 and 66 yards.

The Cowboys have allowed nine plays of 50+ yards this season and 47 of 20+, per Pro Football Reference data.

Schottenheimer met with Parker on Monday afternoon to discuss the challenges.

"It was very honest," Schottenheimer said. "It was very forthright. We have that type of relationship that we can do that. And so, slept on it, picked [it] up again Tuesday morning, having really good conversations, talking about different things. And then the decision was made mid-morning on Tuesday."

Schottenheimer alerted the Cowboys' staff on Tuesday followed by his players on Wednesday. He continued to preach support of Parker even as he demoted him.

Does that mean Parker could get his play-calling job back?

"I mean again, my focus right now is just trying to beat the Titans," Schottenheimer said. "But like I said, I think CP has a very, very bright future as a coach, but more specifically a very bright future here as our defense coordinator. …

"He's a critical piece of what we're trying to do as we search for answers and solutions."

Schottenheimer on his future: 'There's always going to be noise'

The remainder of the Cowboys' season will influence not only Parker's coaching future but also Schottenheimer's.

The Cowboys have not won consecutive games since last November. In two seasons, Schottenheimer has led the team to an 11-15-1 overall record.

An offense featuring Dak Prescott, CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens has flashed high ceilings but inconsistency. A defense that struggled under one-and-done coordinator Matt Eberflus last year has flailed for solutions.

Dallas shifted its defensive structure from a 4-3 to a 3-4 base for the first time in more than a decade this offseason. Personnel has turned over significantly, from trades for interior defensive lineman Quinnen Williams at last year's trade deadline and cornerback Joey Porter Jr. this October, to draft investments that included trading up for first-round safety Caleb Downs and doubling up in the first round with edge rusher Malachi Lawrence.

Missed tackles and communication errors are among the areas Schottenheimer said the team is emphasizing with the message of "doing simple better."

The Cowboys have allowed a league-high 1,350 yards after the catch, per Next Gen Stats. Pro Football Focus, an advanced site that does not know team assignments but does evaluate each team's game film, credits Dallas with 93 missed tackles through 10 games.

For context: PFF credits its top-graded tackling team this season, the Detroit Lions, with 52 missed tackles. PFF's lowest-graded tackling team, the Denver Broncos, have missed 123, per the site. The Cowboys rank 25th in tackling, per PFF.

Can Pettine, who hasn't called defensive plays since 2020, improve the unit?

Schottenheimer credited the 60-year-old as valuable for his perspective on how to use personnel and "really big on affecting the quarterback and pressuring the quarterback and he wants to get the offense unsettled."

Schottenheimer acknowledged his own accountability for the defensive woes, while saying he believes the staff change is a "delicate matter" but ultimately "fair."

When asked if Parker was akin to a young quarterback who could learn from a step back, Schottenheimer said he saw some merit in the comparison but "I don't think Christian Parker's being put on the bench."

Without improvement, Schottenheimer knows questions will grow about whether he will be.

"When you're in this situation and you're the head coach of a 4-6 football team, I mean, you're aware there's always going to be noise," Schottenheimer said. "But I don't focus on that. I really don't. I focus on trying to get these guys ready, trying to get them prepared, and that's my job and my sole responsibility."

articles.title: Ravens' Marlon Humphrey Apologizes for Comments on City of Baltimore on Recent Podcast
articles.summary: Baltimore Ravens cornerback Marlon Humphrey apologized for disparaging remarks he made about the city of Baltimore on his podcast.
articles.body:
Baltimore Ravens cornerback Marlon Humphrey apologized for disparaging remarks he made about the city of Baltimore on his podcast.

"I do know the effect that words have," he told reporters Wednesday. "I'd just like to apologize for those comments."

Humphrey noted he has spent his entire 10-year NFL career in Baltimore and is an "investor" in the city.

Baltimore Mayor Brandon Scott responded in a statement to say "a verbal apology is not enough."

"Baltimore is a city full of young Black boys who look to the Ravens as a beacon of light in their lives and to have someone that looks like them who wears a Baltimore Ravens jersey relegate them to becoming criminals cuts deeper," Scott said.

The mayor also subtly critiqued Humphrey's on-field performance by asking how he would take hearing that "Baltimore once produced great defensive backs but we have recently lost our way."

On the podcast episode, Humphrey was conversing about what Baltimore is known for producing. He mocking said the city is "best at making criminals" (via Glenn Erby of Ravens Wire).

Needless to say, local residents didn't laugh off the pointed comment, and it quickly circulated on social media. The story was big enough that Ravens coach Jesse Minter and safety Kyle Hamilton were asked about it:

Humphrey drew the ire of Ravens fans earlier this month when he said on his podcast they're "always freaking out" and bringing an energy that negatively impacted the players.

The angst is already high with Baltimore sitting at 4-6 and star quarterback Lamar Jackson recovering from his dislocated right thumb. The team could be headed toward a second straight season of missing the playoffs.

Humphrey's broadside against his home market won't help improve the vibes.

articles.title: Joe Milton Reveals Preferred Nickname Highlighting Arm Strength Ahead of Eagles vs. Steelers
articles.summary: Philadelphia Eagles quarterback Joe Milton discussed his nickname preferences ahead of the second start of his career.
articles.body:
Philadelphia Eagles quarterback Joe Milton discussed his nickname preferences ahead of the second start of his career.

Milton, who is known for his arm strength, told reporters Wednesday that he likes to be called "Mr. Rocket" instead of "Bazooka Joe."

"Bazookas only travel so far," he explained.

Milton has operated in a backup role across his three seasons in the NFL, but he's showcased his ability to effortlessly launch deep passes whenever he takes the field.

The 26-year-old is currently serving as Philadelphia's starting quarterback, as Jalen Hurts was ruled out for the remainder of the season following a blood clot diagnosis.

Milton and the Eagles are set to face the Pittsburgh Steelers on Sunday. Kickoff is at 1 p.m. ET.

articles.title: DeVonta Smith Injury Update, Latest on Eagles Star's Status After Missing Last 3 Games
articles.summary: DeVonta Smith is back.
articles.body:
The Philadelphia Eagles wideout told reporters on Wednesday he's completely healthy and ready to go ahead of Sunday's matchup with the Pittsburgh Steelers.

Smith, 28, has been excellent when healthy, catching 26 passes for 310 yards and two touchdowns in four games. His ability to handle the WR1 role and be a difference-maker has made the A.J. Brown trade look even better for the Birds.

The issue, obviously, has been staying on the field. He's missed five games, including the past three, which has played a major part in Philadelphia's 2-7 season. And with Jalen Hurts done for the year and the team trading away several veterans, it seems unlikely the Eagles will be winning many games down the stretch.

Upon his return, Smith will be catching passes from Joe Milton, who has been confirmed as the starter again in Week 11. Milton was 18-of-34 for 169 yards in a 19-11 loss against the New York Giants in Week 9, before the team's bye, taking seven sacks while rushing nine times for 64 yards.

"He works extremely hard with everything," head coach Nick Sirianni told reporters regarding Milton. "Really love his approach, like his personality. But I really appreciate his approach of how he goes through everything. Coaches have done a nice job, Parks (Frazier) has done a nice job. But his approach, he's a really hard worker and I really value that."

Getting Smith back will be a huge boost for Milton. Ditto for getting back fellow wideout Dontayvion Wicks, who has also missed the past three games. Like Smith, Wicks was a limited participant in Wednesday's practice.

articles.title: Two bad teams, one cheap ticket: Jets-Chargers seats barely cost more than a SoFi cheeseburger
articles.summary: Aaron Glenn's New York Jets have lost five straight, and the matchup with the 1-8 Los Angeles Chargers has fans paying just $26 as both teams eye the NFL Draft instead.
articles.body: When you look at the Week 11 slate, there is one game your eyes stop at. You tell your friends and family not to bother you for a few hours during the 4 p.m. slate on Sunday because this matchup is a can’t-miss. articles.title: Cowboys' Quinnen Williams Repeats Same Answer in Trending Video While Discussing Defense, More
articles.summary: Dallas Cowboys star defensive tackle Quinnen Williams didn't have much variety in his answers when discussing the team's struggles on defense during his press conference on Wednesday.
articles.body:
Dallas Cowboys star defensive tackle Quinnen Williams didn't have much variety in his answers when discussing the team's struggles on defense during his press conference on Wednesday.

Williams said "I'm gonna keep that to myself" on 12 separate occasions when speaking to reporters.

The Cowboys sit at just 4-6 this season and own the NFL's No. 30 scoring defense , allowing 28.2 points per game. Dallas is also giving up 6.1 yards per play, ranking No. 31 among all teams (via Pro Football Reference ).

Williams has been one of the few bright spots on the Cowboys' defense, as he's been productive throughout his first full season with the organization.

In 10 games, the four-time Pro Bowler has racked up 46 tackles, 10 quarterback hits, six sacks and three forced fumbles. His 15 tackles for loss are tied for the most in the NFL.

Still, the Cowboys are in danger of missing the playoffs for the third consecutive year unless they can turn their season around.

articles.title: Week 10 Observations: I Like That!
articles.summary: The Season’s Second Act Begins
articles.body:
The Vikings began the unexpected second act of their 2026 season with a resounding 30-10 road victory over the rival Green Bay Packers. Between Kirk Cousins' emotional return and the defense's historic season, it's hard to imagine a more memorable and satisfying result.

The Daily Norseman crew did their usual stellar job recapping the rewarding victory here , here , and here . Aside from the obvious candidates (e.g., Turner, Van Ginkel, Redmond, Smith, Wilson, Van Noy, Price), I was particularly encouraged by contributions from Caleb Banks, Elijah Williams, Gavin Bartholomew, Tai Felton, and Jakobe Thomas. Maybe we do have some depth, huh?

Like He Never Left. Kirk Cousins parachuted into Vikings practice on Wednesday and started on Sunday. As unheard of as that is, given the chaos that's defined the past two seasons at quarterback, seeing him run out to the huddle for the opening series felt totally normal, as if time stood still. I was eagerly soaking it all in.

Even with a few days of prep and a playbook that had changed since 2023, Cousins' familiarity with the scheme and system was evident from the get-go. While the numbers weren't overwhelming – 21 for 31, 207 yards, 2 TDs, and an interception – the eye test was passed with flying colors.

Of course, not all passes and not all yards gained on them are created equal. How and when matter. That's where Cousins immediately changed things. EPA per play improved (+0.04), and the Vikings offense converted 8-of-16 third downs. This included a 3rd-and-23 TD to Myles Price and a critical 3rd-and-12 conversion to Justin Jefferson, who also saw a season-high number of targets. Coincidence? I think not. This was a notable improvement over the 3-for-10 third-down conversion rate in the loss to the Lions and the 3-for-11 in the ugly win against the Colts. The Bills game? Let's not go there.

It's also no fluke that Sunday's game saw the Vikings' offensive time of possession jump to over 35 minutes. This was a marked improvement over the abysmal 17 minutes against the Bills and 24 minutes against the Lions, respectively, in the team's two losses. It was also much better than the 28 minutes in the ugly home win over the hapless Colts. It's almost as if the mere threat of an effective passing game suddenly makes running the ball easier. Weird.

It's just one week, and time will tell, but based on interviews and body language, this seems like a different Kirk Cousins to me. One who is not only more confident and comfortable but also grateful for the opportunity to change the narrative of his career forever – something that seemed out of reach just days earlier. All made easier by what's shaping up to be a historic defense by his side. I basically said it all last week:

Cousins realizes the feel-good, storybook ending is within reach. Reports say the Raiders left the trade decision in his hands. He knows. This is his last, best chance. A Kirk Cousins with a Super Bowl ring would not only have a legitimate Hall of Fame resume (the statistics will be there), but he'd also have a statue outside U.S. Stadium to immortalize his role in ending the long-suffering anguish of a tortured fan base.

I've Seen Enough. This Defense is Generational. After another impressive performance against a top-flight offense, it's time to discuss the 2026 Minnesota Vikings' defense in historic terms.

While national media talking heads usually write narrative checks on the Packers that they inevitably can't cash, it was worse coming into Sunday's game because the Packers had won five of their last six, including a dominant win over a fraudulent Patriots team living off last season's rep the week prior. Instead, they got another kind of check: a reality check.

The eight sacks and four turnovers didn't do justice to the torture Brian Flores inflicted on Matt LaFleur, Jordan Love, and the entire Packers offense throughout the afternoon. It was yet another piece of the puzzle that, when complete, could look record-breaking.

The comparison to the 1985 Bears is impressive enough, especially given the changes made to benefit offenses over the past 20 years.

Enjoy the rest of the ride, folks. Soak it all in, because this isn't normal. It's thrilling, but it's not guaranteed to last beyond this season. Brian Flores will get another head-coaching opportunity someday, and key players such as Blake Cashman, Andrew Van Ginkel, Isaiah Rodgers, and Kyle Van Noy will be free agents. Meanwhile, Jalen Redmond is a restricted free agent, and it's almost certainly Harrison Smith's last hurrah.

Third Time a Charm? Since 1990, the Vikings have made the playoffs 17 times, tying for 7th in that span. Not too shabby. Each year, the purple neurons in my brain lit up, distorting reality into something that justified the belief that they could not only make the Super Bowl but win it.

My intuition has proven far more reliable. It's equipped with the right defenses to filter out most delusions and purify it all. It shocks me back into reality, takes off the blinders so I can see clearly, and acknowledges the issues you know deep down will inevitably dash the dream.

They truly aligned only twice: 1998 and 2009. Not 2000. Not 2017. My gut didn't trust the defense in 2000 or the offense in 2017. In the end, both sides of the ball were an issue, but that doesn't matter now.

What matters is… things are close to aligning with this team again after 17 years. The convergence of multiple elements (i.e., the defense and Cousins' return) for a magical season appears to be in place. There are still eight games left, so that could change before the playoffs, and that very well could happen. But I've never been as close to the long-awaited third instance as I was after this impressive win in Green Bay. A win, or even a razor-thin loss, to the 8-1 49ers next week will put it within arm's reach.

If so, let's hope the third time is the charm and that the season ends with a third act, one that culminates in a Lombardi Trophy triumphantly lifted in the air.

articles.title: 2027 UFL Draft tracker, top prospects as Diego Pavia awaits landing spot
articles.summary: Diego Pavia is among those waiting to hear his name called during the 2027 UFL Draft. Here are the full results from the spring football draft.
articles.body:
The 2027 UFL Draft has arrived, and football fans have one question on their minds heading into the event. Where will former Vanderbilt quarterback Diego Pavia land?

Pavia announced in October he was planning to join the UFL ahead of its 2027 season. The 2025 Heisman Trophy runner-up will instantly become one of the spring football league's biggest stars and will look to prove to all the teams that passed on him in the 2026 NFL Draft that he deserves a chance to play professionally.

While Pavia is the marquee name in the 2027 UFL Draft's player pool, there are plenty of other players with whom football fans will be familiar. A total of 120 players will be selected across the two-day, 15-round event that will help fill out the rosters of the UFL's eight current teams.

Of course, not every player selected is guaranteed to play in the UFL. The spring football draft is a rights draft, meaning teams retain the rights to negotiate with selected players should they choose to play in the UFL.

Still, spring football fans will be eager to see the crop of talent that could be poised to enter the UFL ahead of its 2027 season.

USA TODAY Sports is tracking the results of the 2027 UFL Draft. Follow along with the latest picks and a breakdown of the top prospects available in this year's draft class.

Cheerleaders, celebrities, fans and mascots at NFL games during 2026 season

Results will be added once the draft begins at 8 p.m. ET.

Pavia starred across two seasons at Vanderbilt, leading the Commodores to a winning record in back-to-back seasons. That included a 10-3 mark in 2025, a season during which he completed 70.6% of his passes for 3,539 yards, 29 touchdowns and eight interceptions while adding 862 yards and 10 touchdowns on the ground.

Pavia finished as the runner-up in the 2025 Heisman Trophy voting and signed with the Baltimore Ravens after going undrafted in the 2026 NFL Draft. He was released before the preseason and now will look for a shot to play in the UFL.

Martinez played spring football in 2024, when he won the USFL MVP while a member of the Birmingham Stallions after throwing for 1,748 yards, 15 touchdowns and three interceptions while adding a league-high 528 rushing yards and three scores on the ground. He parlayed that opportunity into a chance with the New York Jets and has spent the last three NFL seasons with the Jets, San Francisco 49ers and Seattle Seahawks.

Currently, Martinez is on the Seahawks' practice squad. It isn't clear whether the 26-year-old will look to return to spring football, but his dual-threat ability will certainly make him a hot commodity should he decide to do so.

Steele went undrafted out of UCLA in 2024 but quickly earned a role in the Kansas City Chiefs' backfield. He totaled 183 yards on 56 carries as a rookie but has only handled one touch, a 4-yard reception, over his last two years with the Chiefs and the Philadelphia Eagles.

Steele (6-0, 228 pounds) is a big-bodied bruiser who runs with great physicality. That could make the 24-year-old a goal-line hammer at the UFL level.

Floriea may not be a household name, but he endeared himself to Cleveland Browns fans during the 2025 and 2026 preseasons. The Kent State product notched a combined seven receptions for 125 yards and three touchdowns across four games of preseason action with the Browns.

Floriea spent the 2025 season on Cleveland's practice squad but failed to earn a spot despite a strong performance in the 2026 preseason. The 25-year-old is small at 5-8, 180 pounds, but his hands and separation skills could make him a quality UFL pass-catcher.

Cunningham, a former Louisville quarterback, began his career as a signal-caller for the Baltimore Ravens and New England Patriots. However, in recent seasons, he transitioned to the receiver position and played one game at the position for the Detroit Lions .

Cunningham, 28, has never attempt a pass nor made a catch at the NFL level, but his dual-threat skill set would make him an intriguing fit for the UFL.

Cunningham isn't the only Louisville product who could draw interest in the UFL draft. Thrash, a 2024 fifth-round pick by the Browns, is in the player pool, and UFL teams would love to get their hands on the speedy 6-0, 190-pound receiver.

Thrash recorded 13 receptions for 129 yards across two seasons with the Browns. He also spent two weeks on the Las Vegas Raiders' practice squad during the 2026 NFL season.

Bell was a seventh-round pick by the Patriots in the 2024 NFL Draft after he enjoyed a standout career at South Carolina and Florida State. Bell made just two catches for 20 yards with the Patriots, but he showed off his upside as a senior with the Seminoles, recording 39 receptions for 503 yards and two touchdowns.

Bell is a bit short for a tight end at 6-2, 241 pounds, but he has a well-rounded skill set that could make him hard to cover for UFL defenders.

Wright's name will be familiar to college football fans, as he tried to become one of the first players to see action with an NFL team and return to the college level. His efforts were denied, leaving Wright in limbo after the Browns waived him and LSU chose not to add him to its roster.

Wright (6-4, 246 pounds) may yet get a chance to play professionally in the UFL. The Ole Miss product had 39 catches for 635 yards and five touchdowns his final season with the Rebels and it's easy to see him developing into a mismatch threat in the spring game.

Pete, like Wright, made headlines during the 2026 NFL preseason. The Kentucky product spent time with the Dallas Cowboys, becoming the first NFL player from the Navajo Nation and earning rave reviews for a locker room speech following Dallas' preseason win over the Arizona Cardinals.

At 6-9, 309 pounds, Pete looks the part of a high-upside, developmental offensive lineman. Developing in the UFL could help him eventually emerge as a contributor thanks to his size alone.

Martin-Rhodes is one of the highest-drafted former NFL players in the 2027 UFL Draft's player pool. He was a third-round pick by the Lions in 2023 but was never quite able to carve out a role during his NFL stops with the Lions and Pittsburgh Steelers.

Martin-Rhodes has just six career tackles and no sacks. The 27-year-old will look to show off his abilities as a run stuffer behind his 6-5, 330-pound frame.

articles.title: 'We apologize': Mike Florio, Chris Simms say sorry after NFL condemns Mike Vrabel 'German mustache' remarks
articles.summary: Mike Florio and Chris Simms have issued a public apology for a PFT Live exchange about Mike Vrabel’s mustache that ended with the NFL condemning the comments...
articles.body:
Mike Florio and Chris Simms have issued a public apology for a PFT Live exchange about Mike Vrabel's mustache that ended with the NFL condemning the comments.

The co-hosts released their contrite statement shortly after 6 p.m. ET Wednesday, roughly 24 hours after the segment streamed on Peacock and only hours after the league publicly denounced the banter that unfolded between the pair during Tuesday's episode.

"On yesterday's (Nov. 17) PFT Live show, we made comments that some found offensive and we apologize."

The statement never says what the comments were or who took offense. Front Office Sports answered the second question earlier Wednesday, as NFL executive vice president Jeff Miller told the outlet that the league considered the remarks "inappropriate and offensive," and a source told FOS that the league had contacted NBC Sports about the segment.

The conversation that set all of this off began innocently enough, with Florio and Simms picking apart the Patriots' loss to the Lions in Munich on Sunday. Florio remarked that Vrabel sounded unusually subdued at his press availability, and Simms put the lethargy down to the transatlantic trip home. Florio then brought up a video from a fan event the night before the game, in which Vrabel was holding what Florio called "a mug bigger than your head," and Simms seized on the Oktoberfest-style imagery to steer the conversation toward the coach's facial hair.

"Yeah, he got the German mustache to go along with that right now, too," Simms said. "So he was hitting all themes there over in Germany."

Florio answered with his own riff on how carefully that mustache would need to be groomed in Germany, and although neither host invoked Hitler by name, TMZ Sports characterized the back-and-forth as a "Hitler joke" in its headline.

"You gotta be careful trimming that thing," Florio said. "Yeah, if you're in Germany, you gotta be careful trimming the sides of that thing."

As the segment went on, producer Gary Carter could be heard groaning off-mic, which prompted Florio to address him and defend the joke before the conversation moved on.

"Gary's groaning. It's funny, Gary," he said. "It was 80 years ago. Let us have some fun, for crying out loud."

Neither Florio nor the Patriots responded to Front Office Sports' requests for comment before the statement was released, and NBC Sports declined to comment. As of Wednesday evening, the audio from the episode had not been taken down. Florio owns ProFootballTalk and licenses it to NBC while keeping editorial control over the site and show, and he also appears on the network's Sunday Night Football studio coverage, but NBC has let him pick which Football Night in America road trips to make this season so that he can work from his West Virginia home studio for the farther games and protect his output on PFT Live and ProFootballTalk.

Simms has continued in his role as Florio's co-host on PFT Live even after NBC removed him from Football Night in America as part of a sweeping overhaul of its Sunday night studio show earlier this year.

Florio and Simms will likely address the controversy further when PFT Live returns Thursday, though it's unclear whether they plan to say anything beyond Wednesday's brief written statement.

articles.title: Ex-Chiefs WR Bub Means signs with Cardinals' practice squad in Week 11
articles.summary: Former Kansas City Chiefs WR Jerrod 'Bub' Means signed with the Arizona Cardinals' practice squad on November 18.
articles.body:
Wide receiver Bub Means signed with the Arizona Cardinals ' practice squad on November 18 after a brief stint with the Kansas City Chiefs .

A former fifth-round pick of the New Orleans Saints in the 2024 NFL Draft, Means played in the Big Easy for two seasons before joining the Cleveland Browns earlier this year. He was waived by Cleveland in early November and signed with the Chiefs on November 5, then spent nearly two weeks in Kansas City before he was waived again on November 17.

NFL insider Aaron Wilson was the first to report Means' latest signing with the Cardinals in a post to his official Twitter account:

Means' acquisition by Arizona comes just days before the Cardinals are set to face the Chiefs in a highly anticipated Week 11 matchup at Arrowhead Stadium, though it is exceedingly unlikely that the former Pittsburgh Panthers standout will be activated from the practice squad so soon after joining his new team.

articles.title: Raiders QB Fernando Mendoza takes responsibility for ‘a lot of sacks’ in NFL debut
articles.summary: Rookie quarterback Fernando Mendoza took his first football loss since 2024. Mendoza drew mixed reviews afterward for his performance against the Seattle Sea...
articles.body:
Rookie quarterback Fernando Mendoza took his first football loss since 2024. Mendoza drew mixed reviews afterward for his performance against the Seattle Seahawks . The Las Vegas Raiders first-time starter even took a lot of sacks in that 21-13 loss Sunday.

But Mendoza didn't point his finger at the offensive line.

Instead he shouldered the blame while addressing reporters on Wednesday.

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

"I'm glad I was able to get out there and create a little bit of a callous, being out there competing with my teammates. And a lot of those sacks were on me," Mendoza said.

Seattle brought the house on Mendoza in creating immense pressure. The Seahawks tallied an astonishing six sacks of the 2025 Heisman Trophy winner.

Seahawks coach Mike Macdonald even turned loose cornerback Devon Witherspoon on blitzes, delivering two sacks . He forced Mendoza into confusion too with an overload look that got Mendoza to check off and call the offensive line to slide the protection toward that side. Except Seattle disguises the look, dropping four into coverage while Witherspoon comes busting through the middle.

Seattle find a way to test Mendoza's mental side in an NFL setting. Mendoza became lauded for his processing ability before facing defenses. But the Seahawks flipped his cerebral side upside down.

So now Mendoza will compartmentalize what went wrong in his league debut. Especially from his personal end in dissecting more coverages and potential blitzes moving forward.

Expect the Denver Broncos to throw something similar at Mendoza. But Denver ranks 27th in total defense despite its 7-2 record.

articles.title: Mike Florio and Chris Simms apologize for 'comments that some found offensive' after being called out by NFL
articles.summary: "PFT Live" hosts Mike Florio and Chris Simms were called out by the NFL for 'inappropriate and offensive' comments about Mike Vrabel's mustache that included...
articles.body:
"PFT Live" hosts Mike Florio and Chris Simms have apologized after being called out by the NFL for making thinly veiled references to Adolf Hitler while joking about Patriots coach Mike Vrabel 's mustache and the team's recent game in Munich.

"On yesterday's (Nov. 17) PFT Live show, we made comments that some found offensive and we apologize," Florio and Simms said in a one-sentence, joint statement released by NBC Sports on Wednesday afternoon.

A day earlier, the hosts were discussing the Patriots on the air when Simms made a comment about Vrabel's "German mustache."

"If you're in Germany, you gotta be careful about trimming the sides of that thing," Florio joked.

"Exactly right," Simms responded. "'Hey, who's that going down the street over there? He put on a few pounds."

Neither of them mentioned the Nazi-era German dictator by name. Nonetheless, an off-camera producer apparently expressed some concerns over the nature of the discussion.

"Gary's groaning," a still-laughing Florio said. "It's funny, Gary! It was 80 years ago. Let us have some fun, for crying out loud."

"We found the remarks inappropriate and offensive," NFL executive vice president for communications and public affairs Jeff Miller said in a statement Wednesday morning.

The NFL has reached out to NBC Sports regarding the matter, according to a league source unauthorized to discuss the matter publicly.

NBC Sports put out a statement Wednesday afternoon.

"On yesterday's (Nov. 17) PFT Live show, there were statements made that were inappropriate," the network said. "Mike and Chris have apologized."

A longtime sports journalist, Florio started the " ProFootballTalk " website in 2001 and sold exclusive rights to its content to NBC in 2009. He has since become a fixture in the network's football coverage, appearing weekly on "Football Night in America" and weighing in as needed as a top NFL insider.

" PFT Live " is housed on NBC's Peacock platform, with episodes five days a week.

This story originally appeared in Los Angeles Times .

articles.title: Former Detroit Lions Pass Rusher Sends Message Before Ford Field Return
articles.summary: Former Detroit Lions pass rusher Al-Quadin Muhammad sends a message ahead of his Ford Field return with the Tampa Bay Buccaneers.
articles.body:
The Detroit Lions will see a couple of familiar faces on the opposite sideline Sunday when they host the Tampa Bay Buccaneers at Ford Field, and one of them has already made it clear what his new team needs to do to win.

Former Lions defensive end Al-Quadin Muhammad , who departed Detroit in free agency after a breakout 2025 season, spoke to reporters Monday about the upcoming matchup. His message was simple: Tampa Bay must find a way to slow down Detroit's explosive rushing attack before worrying about anything else.

According to the Buccaneers' official website , Muhammad emphasized the importance of stopping the run while acknowledging the number of weapons Detroit has on offense.

"Gotta stop the run," said outside linebacker Al-Quadin Muhammad, who was also with the Lions the last two years. "You've gotta stop the run. They have a lot of weapons, they can throw the ball, they can run the ball. First and foremost you have to stop the run and [then] we have to get after the quarterback."

Muhammad also noted that Detroit can hurt opponents through the air and stressed the importance of pressuring the quarterback. Of course, knowing what the Lions want to do and actually stopping them are two very different things.

Al-Quadin Muhammad Returns to Detroit After Breakout Season

Muhammad spent the 2024 and 2025 seasons with the Lions before signing a one-year contract with Tampa Bay in March. The veteran pass rusher enjoyed the best season of his NFL career in 2025, recording 11 sacks, nine tackles for loss, and 20 quarterback hits.

His departure was certainly noteworthy considering how productive he had become in Detroit's defensive rotation. Earlier this year, Muhammad spoke openly about his future with the Lions , explaining how much the opportunity to prove himself meant to his career.

Muhammad won't be the only former Lion making his return to Ford Field, either. Former Detroit captain Alex Anzalone also signed with Tampa Bay during the offseason after spending five seasons helping build Detroit's defense .

Both players know Dan Campbell's team extremely well, and that familiarity could certainly help Tampa Bay prepare for Sunday's matchup.

Buccaneers Face a Tough Challenge Against Jahmyr Gibbs

Muhammad and the Buccaneers have a good reason to make stopping the run their top priority. Jahmyr Gibbs entered the week leading the NFL with 1,000 rushing yards and 11 rushing touchdowns, making him one of the league's most dangerous offensive weapons.

Tampa Bay also enters the matchup with one of the NFL's most impressive run defenses, allowing just 79.1 rushing yards per game. The Buccaneers have held eight consecutive opponents under 100 rushing yards, setting up a fascinating matchup between Detroit's ground attack and Tampa Bay's defensive strength.

According to Tampa Bay's November 16 report , Muhammad and Anzalone both discussed the challenge of stopping Detroit, with Anzalone describing Gibbs as an unusually gifted player who demands special attention.

For Muhammad, Sunday's game offers an opportunity to face the organization where he produced his finest NFL season. For the Lions, it's another chance to show that even players familiar with their offensive system can have a difficult time slowing it down.

And with Gibbs playing the way he has this season, Muhammad and his new teammates certainly have their work cut out for them.

articles.title: Maxx Crosby drops NSFW reason why Raiders still believe in AFC playoff run this season
articles.summary: Maxx Crosby addresses reports that the Raiders are trading Kirk Cousins to start Fernando Mendoza.When the Raiders traded Kirk Cousins to the Vikings during...
articles.body:
When the Raiders traded Kirk Cousins to the Vikings during the NFL trade deadline , the general consensus was that they were punting their season away — even though they were 4-5.

Raiders star defensive end Maxx Crosby would tell you otherwise.

Crosby spoke about the Raiders' decision to move on from Cousins and make way for rookie quarterback Fernando Mendoza on his podcast, "The Rush." He said the team's mindset has not changed.

"We don't look at it as 'Oh, yeah, we're playing for the future.' No, we're playing for now. And we're playing to win now," Crosby said. "That's all you can do. I know the locker room and everybody in that building feels the same way, and we believe in him, and we're gonna rock with him."

Crosby said the Raiders' defense will need to help Mendoza as much as it can, while the offense needs to step up to help him "play good ball."

In Mendoza's first NFL start on Sunday, the Raiders scored on their first offensive possession. Mendoza showed why the team selected him No. 1 overall in the 2026 NFL Draft. He dropped back to pass but decided to keep the ball and scramble up the middle for a 10-yard rushing touchdown.

Coincidentally, the scramble featured shades of his fourth-quarter run in the national title game against Miami in January.

It was the only score the Raiders rookie had in their 21-13 loss to Seattle, but Mendoza showed a lot of promise, completing 17 of 29 passes for 143 yards.

Crosby knows Mendoza has a chance to be special and also knows what he's capable of after going up against him during practice when Mendoza was the Raiders' scout team quarterback.

"He's a robot. He does everything the right way. He's a great f–king kid," Crosby said. "He's extremely talented, he's competitive, he's going to be a great quarterback for a long time."

articles.title: Ravens' Marlon Humphrey apologizes for joking that Baltimore is 'best at making criminals'; mayor requests sit-down with CB
articles.summary: Baltimore Mayor Brandon Scott said in a social media post Wednesday that Humphrey's verbal apology "is not enough."
articles.body:
Marlon Humphrey is currently the longest-tenured defensive player on the Baltimore Ravens. During the latest chapters of his 10-season run with the organization, however, the 30-year-old cornerback's become a lightning rod for criticism.

He received heaps of condemnation after making a derogatory comment on an episode of "The Marlon Humphrey Show" that was released Wednesday.

During a segment on his podcast, Humphrey was asked what Baltimore was best at making. He first mentioned "The Star Spangled Banner" and National Bohemian beer, per ESPN , but then uttered a disparaging line that many have understandably found offensive.

"What is Baltimore best at making?" Humphrey pondered . "They're best at making criminals."

He appeared to be joking, seeming to note that the remark was going to get cut out while laughing. But it wasn't, and it made the rounds on social media. Humphrey then apologized in front of his locker on Wednesday.

"I would like to apologize for some comments on my podcast I had yesterday to the city of Baltimore," Humphrey said, via The Baltimore Banner's Kyle Goon . "As you guys know, I've been here my whole career. Spent lots of offseasons here. Welcomed a son here, and I'm an investor in the city. … And, obviously, I do know the effect that words have and just would like to apologize for those comments."

Later on Wednesday, Baltimore Mayor Brandon Scott said in a social media post that Humphrey's verbal apology "is not enough."

"While we acknowledge Marlon's apology, a verbal apology is not enough," Scott said in his statement . "Baltimore is a city full of young Black boys who look to the Ravens as a beacon of light in their lives and to have someone that looks like them who wears a Baltimore Ravens jersey relegate them to becoming criminals cuts deeper. "I wonder how he would feel if prominent Baltimoreans used their platforms to imply that Baltimore once produced great defensive backs but we have recently lost our way. "They wouldn't do that because our team and city are supposed to be united as one. Baltimore versus the world."

Scott went on to invite Humphrey to sit down with him, as well as a group of Baltimoreans "who have re-entered into our community and are now preventing others from making the mistakes they made."

First-year Ravens head coach Jesse Minter was asked amid his Wednesday news conference if Humphrey's comments were something he deemed worthy of addressing with the veteran corner.

"I think conversations like that remain private between these walls. Just speaking for myself, I love this city," said Minter , who was on Baltimore's staff from 2017-20, years before he received the head job.

"I know what this city means to me and my family and the opportunity that we've been granted here. I take a lot of pride in being here and having been here before and choosing to come back here. It's a great city with a bunch of great people. And we desperately want to represent this city the right way by how we play most importantly."

The Ravens are on a five-game losing streak following their 4-1 start. They've lost quarterbacks Lamar Jackson and Tyler "Snoop" Huntley to significant injuries.

On Monday, they dropped a game in primetime to the previously winless Los Angeles Chargers.

Baltimore fans aren't happy, and many of them have voiced their frustration toward the outspoken Humphrey, who, according to ESPN's Benjamin Solak , has given up the second-most receiving yards in man coverage among corners since the start of last season.

A reporter inquired Wednesday if Humphrey — a 2017 first-round pick, four-time Pro Bowler and two-time first-team All-Pro — is aware of how his reptuation among the fan base has changed over time.

"I try to play my best every Sunday," Humphrey said, via Goon. "That's really all I can do."

Then he was asked if the fans' feelings about him have altered his opinion of them or the city in any way.

"No," Humphrey said. "Not at all. I love the city. I've expressed this many times: I want to win in front of the fans just cause it's not cheap to be in those seats.

"So, no, to answer your question, nothing has changed [with] how I feel."
